Cluster 5 · IPM, FRAC Rotation & CIB&RC / EU MRL Compliance

Grape Downy Mildew, Powdery Mildew, Thrips, Mealybugs & EU MRL Rules

Direct Answer · Grape Diseases, Pests & EU MRL Safety

Downy Mildew (Kevda) and Powdery Mildew (Bhuri) dominate Indian vineyards alongside Flea Beetle, Thrips, and Mealybugs. Pair Extended Y-Trellis airflow with FRAC/IRAC rotation and Cryptolaemus biocontrol, strictly obeying ICAR-NRCG Annexure-5 PHIs and avoiding CIB&RC-banned pesticides and late Phosphonates/Mancozeb [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA 2026].

Mandatory CIB&RC Banned Chemicals & EU GrapeNet MRL Red List

Direct Answer · Banned Pesticides & EU Rejection Triggers

CIB&RC BANNED in India: Dichlorvos, Monocrotophos, Carbofuran, and Phorate. Top EU GrapeNet MRL Rejection Triggers: Chlormequat Chloride (CCC), Fosetyl-Al / Phosphonic acid, Mancozeb, Carbendazim, Acephate, and late Chlorpyrifos. Also flag Streptocycline antibiotic restrictions — verify current-season ICAR-NRCG Annexure-5 before every spray [DPPQ&S; APEDA 2026].

CIB&RC BANNED · ZERO USE

Prohibited Molecules (DPPQ&S India)

  • Dichlorvos (DDVP) — Banned
  • Monocrotophos — Banned / Restricted
  • Carbofuran — Banned
  • Phorate — Banned
  • Streptocycline — Antibiotic restrictions apply; verify label status before any bacterial leaf spot spray
EU MRL FAILURE TRIGGERS · ANNEXURE-5

Stop Early or Avoid in Export Lots [APEDA; NRCG]

  • CCC (Lihocin) — Replace with mechanical 5–7 leaf sub-cane pinching
  • Fosetyl-Al / Phosphonic acid & Mancozeb — Long persistence; halt early per Annexure-5 PHI
  • Carbendazim & Acephate — High EU border rejection risk
  • Chlorpyrifos — Trunk stem-borer plug (5 ml/L) ONLY; NEVER spray near berries!
  • Imidacloprid — Bud-break Flea Beetle ONLY (60d+ EU PHI)

Visual "Photo Look-Alike" Vineyard Triage Cards

Direct Answer · Look-Alike Disease & Disorder Triage

Compare confusing field symptoms side-by-side before spraying: Downy Mildew (yellow upper oil spots + underside white fluff) vs Powdery Mildew (ash-grey dust + berry cracking), and Dogridge Na⁺ Scorch vs Botryosphaeria Arm Dieback (no systemic cure — prune back to clean white-green wood) [ICAR-NRCG].

Fungal Leaf & Bunch Triage
CURABLE · ACT IN <24 HRS

Downy Mildew (Kevda)

Plasmopara viticola
  • Translucent yellow "oil spots" on UPPER leaf surface
  • Fluffy white cottony spore growth strictly on LOWER surface
  • Wet Oct rain turns entire young flower panicle brown/twisted
Field Fix: Strip low shaded leaves; rotate Copper (2 g/L), Dimethomorph (1 g/L) + Mancozeb, Mandipropamid, or Cymoxanil+Mancozeb. Stop Phosphonates & Mancozeb early for EU MRL PHI [ICAR-NRCG].
CURABLE · DRY WEATHER

Powdery Mildew (Bhuri)

Erysiphe necator
  • Ash-grey dusty powder on BOTH leaf surfaces & green canes
  • Floury grey coating on berries -> scarred skin -> vertical berry cracking
  • Thrives in dry, warm, shaded Y-trellis/Bower interiors
Field Fix: Pull cluster-zone leaves for airflow; Wettable Sulphur (2 g/L — stop above 32–35°C!), rotate Myclobutanil (0.4 g/L), Azoxystrobin, or Potassium bicarbonate near harvest [ICAR-NRCG].
Vine Decline & Cordon Death Triage
MANAGEABLE · SWITCH TO 110R

Dogridge Na+ Toxicity / K-Mg Scorch

Saline Water (ECw >1.0 dS/m, Na+)
  • Marginal leaf scorching + interveinal yellowing on older leaves
  • Petiole test shows Na >0.40–0.50% or Cl >1.0–1.5% alongside low K/Mg
  • Gradual cordon weakening in Year 4–5 on Dogridge under saline borewells
Field Fix: Auto-block MOP immediately; switch to SOP (0:0:50) + 0.5–1% MgSO4 + gypsum + 10–15 t/ha mulch + water pH 6.5 acidification. Replant saline blocks on 110R / B2-56 [ICAR-NRCG].
NO SYSTEMIC CURE · PRUNE WOOD

Arm Dieback / Trunk Canker

Botryosphaeria spp.
  • Sudden wilting/death of one entire spur, arm, or cordon
  • Cross-section cut of wood shows dark brown wedge-shaped necrosis
  • Often enters through unprotected April/October pruning cuts
Field Fix: Cut back ruthlessly until cross-section shows 100% clean white-green wood. Immediately seal every cut with Copper oxychloride / Bordeaux wound paste + Trichoderma [ICAR-NRCG].
Small / Scarred Berry Triage
PREVENTABLE · PRE-BLOOM B+Zn

Shot Berries (Boron / Zinc / Cold)

Micronutrient Deficiency or Late Nov Prune
  • Many tiny pea-sized green berries remain mixed beside normal berries
  • Smooth skin (no corky rings) — caused by poor pollination/fertilization
  • Worse when Oct pruning slips into late Nov cold or B/Zn is deficient
Field Fix: Spray 0.1% Boron + 0.25% Zinc pre-bloom (verify water B <1 ppm!). Keep Oct pruning in optimal window and confirm 45 DAP petiole B & Zn at 30–50 ppm [ICAR-NRCG].
CURABLE · EARLY IPM (<8 mm)

Thrips Scab / Russet Ring

Scirtothrips dorsalis / Rhipiphorothrips
  • Corky brown halo/scab ring around berry stem end or sides
  • Silvery curled young leaf tips at pre-bloom to 8 mm stage
  • Rejects EU export lots visually even when Brix is >=16°
Field Fix: Install 25 blue sticky traps/ha at sprout; when >5 thrips/shoot, rotate Spinosad (0.25–0.3 ml/L) or Emamectin benzoate (0.22–0.4 g/L) strictly within NRCG Annexure-5 PHI [ICAR-NRCG].
Veraison & Post-Harvest Berry Triage
CANOPY FIX · NOT FUNGAL

Pink Berry Syndrome

Abiotic Sun + Cold-Night / Warm-Day Swing
  • Unwanted pink/blush pigmentation on white Thompson Seedless clusters
  • Concentrated on sun-exposed outer bunches during Jan–Feb temperature swings
  • Berries stay intact on pedicel but lose uniform green-amber export grade
Field Fix: Maintain diffused Y-trellis leaf canopy shade, skirt/paper-bag exposed bunches, and maintain balanced K/Ca nutrition without excess late N [ICAR-NRCG].
IRREVERSIBLE + EU MRL RISK

CPPU Overdose Shatter & Cracking

CPPU >2 ppm / Late N / Irregular Drip
  • Abnormally thick crunchy berry skin, delayed sugar (<16°Brix), loose pedicels
  • Berries split vertically after uneven veraison watering or drop inside export box
  • CPPU >2 ppm triggers EU MRL failure and post-harvest shatter
Field Fix: NEVER exceed 1–2 ppm CPPU (strictly once). Keep veraison drip steady (8–12 L/vine/day), supply early Tank-B Calcium, pre-cool 4–6 hrs to 0–1°C, and pack with dual-release SO2 pads [APEDA].

Major Grapevine Diseases & FRAC Rotation Matrix

Direct Answer · Downy Mildew, Powdery Mildew, Anthracnose & Dieback

Control Downy Mildew by stripping low shaded leaves and rotating Copper (2 g/L), Bordeaux (0.5–1%), Dimethomorph + Mancozeb, and Mandipropamid. Control Powdery Mildew with Wettable Sulphur (2 g/L, stop >32–35°C), Myclobutanil, Azoxystrobin, and late-safe Potassium bicarbonate [ICAR-NRCG].

Major Vineyard Pests, ETLs, Biocontrol & CIB&RC Safe Options

Direct Answer · Grape Pest IPM & Biocontrol

Act at exact thresholds: Flea Beetle (>5/vine at 7–25 DAP), Thrips (>5/shoot pre-bloom to 8 mm with 25 blue sticky traps/ha), Mealybug (bark strip + ant band + 1,500–2,500/ha Cryptolaemus beetles Nov–Dec), and Spider Mites (>5/leaf Jan–Apr) [ICAR-NRCG Annexure-5].

Grape Disease, Pest & EU MRL FAQs

How do you tell Downy Mildew (Kevda) apart from Powdery Mildew (Bhuri) in the vineyard?

Downy Mildew shows translucent yellow oil spots on the UPPER leaf surface with fluffy white cottony spores strictly UNDERNEATH during wet weather. Powdery Mildew forms ash-grey dry dust on BOTH leaf sides and berries, causing vertical cracking [ICAR-NRCG].

Which pesticides cause the most EU GrapeNet MRL rejections or are banned by CIB&RC?

CIB&RC BANNED pesticides include Dichlorvos, Monocrotophos, Carbofuran, and Phorate. Top EU MRL failure triggers are Chlormequat Chloride (CCC), Fosetyl-Al/Phosphonic acid, Mancozeb, Carbendazim, and late Chlorpyrifos. Always check current-season ICAR-NRCG Annexure-5 PHIs [APEDA; DPPQ&S].

How do you control Mealybug without leaving pesticide residues near harvest?

Strip loose trunk bark, apply a sticky ant-barrier trunk band, apply Buprofezin (1.25–1.5 ml/L) or Spirotetramat early, and release predator beetles Cryptolaemus montrouzieri at 1,500–2,500/ha in Nov–Dec. Never spray Chlorpyrifos near berries [ICAR-NRCG].

How do you manage Flea Beetle (Udadya) during bud sprouting?

Monitor swollen buds at 7–25 DAP (ETL > 5 beetles/vine). Strip bark and clear vineyard trash pre-pruning; apply Imidacloprid (0.3–0.4 ml/L) or Lambda-cyhalothrin strictly at bud-break because of their 60d+ EU PHI [ICAR-NRCG].
